ABSTRACT:


This

study

aimed

to

investigate

how

the

in

The

question

“Can

the

body

in

motion

in

dance

have

a

writing

effect,

on

the

assumption

that

it

produces

a

channeling

of

meaning

from

which

the

signifier

emerges?”

led

to

a

theoretical-clinical

discussion

regarding

the

body

in

motion

through

dance

as

a

possibility

for

the

subject

to

construct

a

border

around

the

void

in

reality

produced

by

trauma.

This

research

was

inspired

by

a

work

experience

conducted

in

a

psychiatric

inpatient

unit

at

a

public

hospital,

where

dance

and

body

awareness

workshops

were

held.

The

proposal

arose

from

the

need

to

find

a

way

to

address

what

was

described

by

service

users

and

staff

as

“aggressiveness”

or

“aggressive

impulses.”

After

the

first

workshops,

discussion

circles

emerged

about

how

the

participants

felt,

during

which

they

associated

feelings

and

memories

with

the

movements.

From

this,

the

hypothesis

arose

that

something

from

the

unconscious

was

set

in

motion

when

the

body

began

to

move

in

dance.

From

the

content

shared

during

these

moments,

using

the

psychoanalytic

research

method,

material

was

produced

that

served

as

the

basis

for

the

analysis

supporting

this

discussion.

This

material

is

in

written

form

and

was

compiled

by

re-reading

personal

notes

taken

after

the

workshops

during

the

period

of

the

aforementioned

experience,

as

well

as

memories

that

emerged

during

the

process

of

re-reading.

From

this

process

emerged

clinical

fragments,

which

were

analyzed

based

on

the

interplay

between

Freudian-Lacanian

theoretical

frameworks

on

the

body,

trauma,

and

the

written

word,

as

well

as

the

signifiers

that

persistently

recurred,

evoked

in

the

transference

with

the

material.

As

a

consequence

of

this

analysis,

the

hypothesis

emerged

that

something

from

the

unconscious

was

set

in

motion

with

effects

similar

to

those

of

writing.

In

some

way,

the

body

in

motion

during

dance

seems

to

have

offered

the

subjects

a

support

to

cross

the

threshold

from

the

register

of

experience

to

the

word,

what

produces.

the

in

motion

during

functioned

as

a

supportive

mechanism,

of

associations

and

movement,

producing

new

the

construction

a

narrative
